Lesson 7 · Past Simple
Lesson 7
Talking About the Past
Past Simple — Regular & Irregular Verbs
🕰️📅✍️
🎯 Get ready

Lesson Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  • 1 Talk about actions that happened in the past.
  • 2 Recognize the difference between regular and irregular verbs.
  • 3 Use common time expressions correctly.
  • 4 Build sentences about yesterday, last week, and last year.
  • 5 Ask and answer simple questions about the past.
🗣️ Warm-up

Let's Talk First

Tap a question to see a sample answer idea.

What did you do yesterday? ▸
Sample ideaI stayed home and watched a movie.
Did you have a good weekend? ▸
Sample ideaYes, I visited my family and relaxed a lot.
What was the last movie you watched? ▸
Sample ideaI watched an action movie last weekend.
Where did you go last weekend? ▸
Sample ideaI went to the mall with my friends.
🖼️ Picture

Look & Describe

Where are they now? ▸
SampleThey are sitting in a coffee shop.
What are they looking at? ▸
SampleThey are looking at photos on a phone.
Where do you think they went yesterday? ▸
SampleI think they went hiking in the mountains.
Did they enjoy the trip? ▸
SampleYes, they look very happy in the photo.

🔍 Look and Think

Read the Sentences

  • 1 I went to the mall yesterday.
  • 2 She bought a new phone.
  • 3 They watched a movie last night.
  • 4 We visited our grandparents.
  • 5 He found his wallet.
  • 6 They developed a new app.
Are these actions happening now? ▸
ThinkNo. They happened in the past — the actions started and finished before now.
📖 Grammar

Past Simple

We use the Past Simple to talk about actions that started and finished in the past.
✔ Most verbs add -ed.
❗ Many common verbs change completely — these are called irregular verbs.
📖 Grammar

Time Expressions

Words that tell us the action is finished.

yesterday yesterday morning yesterday afternoon last night last week last month last year two days ago an hour ago in 2024
📖 Grammar

1. Irregular Verbs

These verbs do not follow a rule.

go → went
eat → ate
buy → bought
see → saw
find → found
hear → heard
come → came
leave → left
feel → felt
think → thought
📖 Grammar

2. Regular Verbs

Most verbs simply add -ed.

watch → watched
clean → cleaned
finish → finished
move → moved
call → called
help → helped
arrive → arrived
visit → visited
discover → discovered
recommend → recommended
📖 Grammar

Example Sentences

  • ✓ Yesterday, I went to work.
  • ✓ She bought a new laptop.
  • ✓ We watched a football match.
  • ✓ My brother helped me.
  • ✓ The company developed a new website.
  • ✓ I recommended this restaurant to my friend.
  • ✓ They discovered an interesting place.

✍️ Exercise 5 · 1 of 2

Rewrite in the Past

Tap to check the past-tense sentence.

She studies English every evening. ▸
AnswerShe studied English last evening.
We take the bus to work every morning. ▸
AnswerWe took the bus to work yesterday morning.
My friend buys fresh bread from the bakery. ▸
AnswerMy friend bought fresh bread from the bakery.
They organize charity events every year. ▸
AnswerThey organized a charity event last year.
✍️ Exercise 5 · 2 of 2

Rewrite in the Past

Tap to check the past-tense sentence.

The manager explains the project to new employees. ▸
AnswerThe manager explained the project to the new employees.
I make coffee before I start work. ▸
AnswerI made coffee before I started work.
The engineer solves difficult technical problems. ▸
AnswerThe engineer solved a difficult technical problem.
My parents invite our relatives for dinner. ▸
AnswerMy parents invited our relatives for dinner.

✍️ Exercise 7 · 1 of 2

Unscramble the Sentences

Tap to check the correct word order.

yesterday / went / I / the museum / with my cousins / to ▸

recommended / my teacher / an excellent book / for beginners ▸
AnswerMy teacher recommended an excellent book for beginners.
the students / completed / before the deadline / the project ▸
AnswerThe students completed the project before the deadline.

AnswerThe volunteers organized a community clean-up campaign last Saturday.
